issues.description: The entity ID type for Person is inconsistent between template and solution repositories and also inconsistent within the solution file itself. In the template, Person.id is declared as Long (template_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java lines 19-22) and the repositories (JpaRepository<Person, Long>) expect a Long id. In the solution, the Person class declares the id field as Integer but the getter and setter use Long (solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java lines 22 and 53-59). Additionally, PersonRepository in the solution still uses JpaRepository<Person, Long>, which does not match the Integer field. This type mismatch will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended ID type (Long vs Integer), preventing them from correctly understanding/using the repository and entity.
issues.suggested_fix: Pick a single ID type and apply it consistently across entity, repository, and accessors. The simplest fix (and consistent with the template) is to change the id field in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java from Integer to Long, and ensure the getter and setter use Long. Confirm JpaRepository<Person, Long> remains the repository type. This aligns solution code with the template and the repository generic type and removes compilation/type confusion for students.
